newsitem.title: USA: Kirby Corp says Miss. floods hurt Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Kirby Corp says Miss. floods hurt Q1 net.

text.p: Kirby Corporation said Tuesday that flooding on the Mississippi River hurt net income during the first quarter of 1977, depressing earnings per share to $0.19 cent versus $0.20 cent during the 1996 quarter.
The marine transportation company reported net earnings for the 1997 quarter of $4,739,000 compared with $5,240,000 seen during the same quarter last year.

"During the month of March, the lower Mississippi River, Kirby's principal area of operations, experienced high water conditions not seen in such severity since 1983, resulting in significant reductions in inland fleet efficiency," the company said in a prepared statement.

"During the first quarter, Kirby generally experienced high water and flooding conditions in the upper Mississippi River and Ohio River, resulting in river closures in selected areas for numerous days and mandated regulatory restrictions," it added.
The 1997 first quarter included a $2,000,000 redemption of Universal Insurance Company common stock and a $1,039,000 distribution from a marine partnership, totaling $.12 per share, it said.
The company said since January 1, 1997, it had purchased 580,650 shares of its common stock at a total purchase price of $10,887,000, an average price of $18.75 per share.

Since 1995, when the current repurchase program began, it said the company had purchased 4,391,000 shares of its common stock, leaving 24,904,000 shares remaining at the end of the recent first quarter.
